name: Leather watch strap

card.summary: A leather band for a wristwatch that gives the watch a dressier, more classic look and makes it easy to match to a suit or smart outfit.
card.note: Leather can absorb sweat and moisture and may need replacing; metal-free straps can help people with metal contact dermatitis.

quick.overview:
A leather watch strap attaches a watch to the wrist and is the traditional choice for dress and pilot-style watches. It helps looks by pairing a watch with formal or smart-casual clothing and softening the sportier feel of a steel bracelet or rubber band.
Because watches attach with standard spring bars, the strap can be swapped without changing the watch, so one watch can look different across occasions. Most of the material is style commentary from forums.
quick.how: Men on forums describe wearing a plain watch on a black leather strap as an understated dressy option, and saving a flashier watch for special occasions. Straps are changed by swapping spring bars; colours such as black or brown are the usual matches for formal clothes.
quick.risks: Leather can wear, discolour or hold odour with sweat and water, and animal-product concerns lead some to choose alternatives. Metal watch bracelets can cause contact dermatitis in some people, and non-metal straps such as leather or NATO-style are mentioned as an option for them.

lead: A watch strap, also called a band, secures a wristwatch to the wrist and works as both a practical part and a fashion item. Leather is common for dress and pilot-style watches [1].

In style discussion on T Nation, men describe a plain watch on a black leather strap as a restrained everyday choice, with a bigger statement watch kept for special occasions, and name brands such as Longines and Breitling paired with black leather [2][3]. Another poster says a watch should reflect lifestyle, with a classic look for a bank job and a sportier one for athletes [4].
Straps attach to the case with spring bars, a standard system that makes swapping straps easy [1].

chain: Fit a leather strap to the watch
Watch reads as dressy and classic
angle.text: Swapping to leather shifts the watch from sporty to dressy, so the wrist accessory fits a suit or smart outfit. The change lasts as long as the strap is worn.

paras: Leather straps are common on dress and pilot-style watches. A bund strap has two leather layers with a separate piece against the wrist, which originally protected skin in hot cockpits [1].
Other strap materials include stainless steel, rubber, silicone, cloth and nylon NATO straps, the latter introduced by the UK Ministry of Defence in 1973 [1].

Men's style threads on T Nation treat a leather-strapped watch as a classic dressy choice [2][3]. One poster writes that a watch is the only jewellery a man should wear and should reflect his style [4].

Metal watches and straps can cause contact dermatitis, and strap styles that keep metal off the skin can help affected wearers [1]. A microbiology paper isolated a fungus, Aspergillus versicolor, from a leather watch strap and tested industrial biocides against it, showing that leather can host mould [5].
No studies found. A laboratory paper tested fungicides on a mould isolated from a leather watch strap, but it did not study wearers [5].

timeline.event: UK Ministry of Defence introduces the NATO strap, a nylon alternative to leather [1].

refs.title: Evaluation of Industrial Biocides on a Novel Aspergillus versicolor TANCK-1 and Elucidation of Their Probable Biocidal Mechanism.
